what: the four execution models on the same workload, 2000 events/s offered

fixed.data: 1k_seed3 control, cycled by the load generator

equivalence_check: all four published 3684-3685 updates, so they did the same work

statefun.notes: state shipped with each invocation; checkpointing on

ray_actors.notes: state in actor heap; no managed state, no recovery, roads sharded across actors by hash because one actor per road would need one OS process per road

flink_keyed_per_minute.notes: open minute kept in the operator, Flink state touched at minute close only; loses the minute in progress on failure

flink_keyed_per_event.notes: faithful translation: all twin state in Flink, read and written per event. 91% of the time is Python-to-JVM state access at about 1.5 ms per access

caveat: the keyed numbers are PyFlink's cost for Python state access, not Flink keyed state in general; a Java implementation would avoid the boundary but cannot run scikit-learn models
